With `close - open - 1` the scan resumes two characters early, inside the interval: only its last digit or comma and the closing '}' are re-read, plain characters the scanner's default branch skips, so the verdict is the same.
`close` is indexOf('}', open) where pattern[open] is '{', so it is -1 or greater than open >= 0, never 0: `close < 0` and `close <= 0` agree.
The extra outer iteration (a == branches.size) runs an empty inner loop (`a + 1 until size`) and reads no branch, so the result is the same.
